newsitem.title: UK: Cobalt traders digest latest Gecamines directive.
newsitem.headline: Cobalt traders digest latest Gecamines directive.

text.p: A circular to customers from Zaire's copper/cobalt producer Gecamines -- recently taken over by rebels -- contained a reference to existing contracts which was causing concern, cobalt traders said.
The circular, in French, included the sentence: "Previous commitments of the Commercial Directorate which have not yet been executed have to be confirmed by the new chairman."
Gecamines offices in Europe were not available for comment.

Traders said that on the face of it Gecamines' new Commercial Directorate based in Lubumbashi in the rebel-controlled Shaba mining region wanted confirmation from consumers that they would honour existing contracts.
But other traders expressed concern that it could mean that the new management was looking to renegotiate contracts on more favourable terms to the seller.
The price of high-grade cobalt has risen to around $26 a lb on the European free-market from around $20 in February.
Rebels led by Laurent Kabila appointed a new head of the state mining giant after they captured Lubumbashi in April.

The circular, obtained by Reuters, also included confirmation the Commercial Directorate was now located in Lubumbashi and that the new chairman of the Directorate was Sungu Tshofu, previously chief-engineer of Gecamines' General Delegation.
All commitments by the Commercial Directorate will have to be seen or signed by the chairman, the circular said.
